## 95315dd52287

**Reproduced distribution shortcut plus canonical-domain validator mismatch.**
This conclusion is bound to generator SHA-256
`ee41ee644c95c867340523295ec5140835e00dc64d18a23df69a0f82d0bf2e01`
and executed Racket rule hash `14aa51e44193`.

Across 60 generated inputs—20 each from easy, medium, and hard—the source always
placed the same normalized three-cell L shape `[(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)]` at source
origin `(0,0)`, with exactly two blob colors. A deliberately wrong rival ignores
the observed source geometry, reads the three blob values row-major, and pastes
them at that one memorized orientation. It matched **60/60** authoritative Racket
outputs from the generated distribution but only **2/3** canonical labels. On
canonical train pair 1, the authoritative crop-and-translate output preserves
orientation `[(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)]`; the rival rotates it into the memorized shape.
The small counterexample was also run through the supported Racket apply command,
and its output hash matches the canonical label.

The validator separately rejects two of its three own canonical inputs because
it gratuitously requires at least two blob colors; those canonical cases use one
color and are valid for the authoritative rule. The advertised `grid_h=5` exact
value also raises because generation internally restricts it to 6–9, and unknown
overrides are silently ignored. Generated probe inputs are within the current
source's documented domain and pass its validator; the canonical counterexample
belongs to the authoritative task domain but is wrongly rejected by that
validator.
